en-US.shortDescription: Medication reminders with safety guardrails, daily check-ins with symptom escalation, and a family dashboard. Coordination and reminders, not medical advice.
en-US.fullDescription:
CareCompanion helps an older adult and their family keep track of medications and how the day is going, with safety guardrails built in.

For the person at home: ask what is on the plan today, say when you have taken a medication in your own words ("my blood pressure pill"), tell CareCompanion how you are feeling, or ask for help. A dose guard refuses a duplicate or too-soon dose until you explicitly confirm and give a reason, and it lets your family know. Symptoms are graded: a mild complaint is noted, an urgent one alerts your caregivers, and an emergency comes back with guidance you hear first.

For family caregivers: ask how Mom is doing this week and get a spoken summary plus the live family dashboard rendered right inside Alexa+ (adherence over 7 or 30 days, today's doses, open alerts, the check-in trend and upcoming appointments). Add a medication and CareCompanion reads back any warnings from its curated interaction and allergy list. Acknowledge or resolve alerts with a note so everyone can see who handled what.

CareCompanion is a coordination and reminder tool, not medical advice. Warnings are informational; always follow the instructions of your doctor or pharmacist, and in an emergency call your local emergency number. This release runs a fictional demo household (Eleanor Whitfield, 78, and her caregivers Priya and Daniel) with synthetic data: there are no accounts and no personal data is collected. Open source under the MIT license: https://github.com/skiitk2510/carecompanion
examplePhrases: Alexa, I took my blood pressure pill
Alexa, I'm feeling a bit dizzy
Alexa, how is Mom doing this week
